properties.description: Seven cases across two files. CORE (crates/reflow2-core/tests/record_change_can_state_its_axis.rs, 3): a subject stated on ChangeRecord reaches the stored event, on BOTH values so the check cannot pass against a hardcoded one, and an omitted subject stays absent. SERVED SURFACE (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/record_change_carries_the_axis.rs, 4): the same three through the tool, plus a value outside the enum refused with the parameter named and NOTHING written — a partial event would be worse than the refusal. THE SPLIT IS THE POINT, NOT DUPLICATION: the original defect was a field that existed in Rust and could not be reached by the caller who needed it, so a core-only check would re-create exactly the condition being fixed. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ASSERTED AS ABSENCE: the third case in each file pins that `resync` — the change type whose axis genuinely cannot be derived — still stores no subject when none was given. Inference is the failure this field exists to avoid, and a default value would reintroduce it silently.
properties.findings: 7 of 7 passing. Run against the built binary as well as the library: the served cases go through ReflowService, and toolsnap confirms `subject` is on the published record_change schema (one golden changed, nine lines, nothing else moved). The refusal case was checked to reject `sistem` by naming "change subject" and to leave no ChangeEvent behind.
properties.name: record_change carries the caller's axis, at the core and at the served tool
